tools.name: get_composite
tools.description: Everything the platform knows about one ticker in a single record: the cross-signal consensus, each contributing dimension with its direction and provenance, and risk flags. Start here for any question about a specific company.

tools.name: get_demo_composite
tools.description: A single fixed demo ticker, callable without an API key, so the data shape can be inspected before signing up. Returns only the demo ticker regardless of input. For real tickers use get_composite, which requires a free key.

tools.name: get_evidence
tools.description: Paid key required. The primary documents a ticker's signals were derived from — insider Form 4s, institutional holdings and macro series, with the filing each came from where one is available. Use this to cite a claim rather than assert it. Paid keys are not on sale yet. A ticker whose evidence has

tools.name: get_house_rating
tools.description: Paid key required. The platform's own buy/hold/sell rating for a ticker, with the reasoning behind it. A judgement about the stock, not a recommendation to any reader. Paid keys are not on sale yet.

tools.name: get_consensus
tools.description: Whether the independent actors this platform tracks — insiders, Congress, institutions, the model — agree on one ticker, with the per-dimension breakdown that produced the verdict.

tools.name: rank_consensus
tools.description: The names where independent actors agree most strongly, ranked. Use this to find candidates rather than to check one you already have in mind.

tools.name: screen
tools.description: Filter the whole equity universe and return matching tickers with their scores. The bulk discovery tool: use it for questions of the form 'which companies have X'. To rank by cross-signal agreement instead, use rank_consensus.

tools.name: get_monthly_activity
tools.description: Rank ticker activity aggregated from available published filings by transaction date for the current UTC month through today. Includes coverage metadata and unknown-value counts; this is not total market activity. Congress: 10 names on every customer key. Insiders: free keys receive up to 10 names,

tools.name: list_insider_trades
tools.description: Corporate insider buys and sells from SEC filings, newest first, with a link to the filing each came from where one is available.

tools.name: list_congress_trades
tools.description: Disclosed House and Senate trades, newest first, linked to the disclosure where one is available. Up to 20 rows per call on every customer key; page with next_cursor.

tools.name: list_positioning
tools.description: Weekly speculative positioning in FUTURES markets from the CFTC Commitments of Traders report, newest first: net speculative position, its share of open interest and its historical percentile. Covers futures symbols such as ES (S&P 500 e-mini), GC (gold), ZT (2-year Treasury note), not individual st

tools.name: get_historic_moves
tools.description: The historical distribution of 5-day and 1-month returns for a ticker, sampled over the last 5 years: mean, standard deviation, percentiles, a histogram, and the worst drawdowns with their dates. Use it to say whether a move is unusual FOR THIS NAME rather than in the abstract. Every number is a fra

tools.name: list_equity_perp
tools.description: Funding rate and open interest for the ~51 US single names listed on a 24/7 perpetual futures venue, ranked by notional. This is the ONLY source here that moves outside US market hours, so it is what to check overnight and at weekends. High positive funding means longs are paying to hold — crowded,

tools.name: get_equity_perp
tools.description: Funding and open interest for a single name on the 24/7 perpetual venue. Most tickers are NOT listed there — only about 51 of about 4,600 covered tickers — and a 'not listed' answer means no venue coverage, never that positioning is flat or zero.

tools.name: search_tickers
tools.description: Resolve a company name or partial symbol to tickers the platform covers. Use this first when the user names a company rather than a symbol.

tools.name: get_signal
tools.description: A whole-market gauge rather than a per-company one. 'macro' is the market-regime read, 'energy' the macro energy balance, 'crypto' crypto positioning and funding, 'rate_expectations' the market-implied path for policy rates. Use these for the backdrop a single name is trading against.
